children: faces a big delivery test heading into year-end, with fourth-quarter sales guidance calling for roughly 3 billion more revenue than the previous quarter. U.S.-listed shares stood at $1,669.63, up 1.71%, as of approximately 12.54 p.m. ET on October 19. According to an AD HOC NEWS report, Citi raised its price target to 2,300 from 2,200 on October 15 and maintained its Buy rating. That adds bullish backing. Delivering the machines is the next test.

ASML's October 14 results set fourth-quarter sales guidance at 14.2 billion to 15.2 billion, following 11.662 billion in the third quarter. Hitting the 14.7 billion midpoint would require a 26.1% sequential jump. Management expects gross margin around 57%, slightly below the third quarter's 57.5%. Demand looks strong: the company says its planned supply cannot fully meet customers' needs in 2027 and 2028, and it is investigating further capacity expansion.

The valuation leaves less room for mistakes. The GF Value comparison puts the shares 25.69% above estimated fair value, suggesting investors already pay a premium for future growth. That does not establish where the stock goes next. It does raise the stakes for execution. The immediate question is whether ASML can turn its demand pipeline into recognized sales while meeting its margin forecast. More capacity could support years of growth, but orders, deliveries and profits still have to line up.

title: ASML Stocks Rise 1.7% Although Its AI Outlook Demands a 26% Sales Jump
